transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I guess I'm here because... well, I've started doing things at work and school lately that just don't really make sense. Like, at work—I do bookkeeping—I've been taking all the receipts and just lining them up all the way across the floor. We get so many receipts from this one hardware store, and they use that weird thermal paper, you know? The kind that turns black if you scratch it with your fingernail. I used to do that all the time when I was a kid when my mom would take me to the grocery store. I'd draw little smiley faces on the back of the receipt while she was loading the car. She always used those canvas bags way before it was a trendy thing to do... 

But yeah, I just line them up on the floor. Or I'll sit at my desk and just tap the calculator in sets of nine. Always nine. And then sometimes I'll go over and just stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, just frozen there, until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay. It's a really old copier, actually, it makes this loud humming noise and jams every time you try to print double-sided... but anyway, yeah, people have been looking at me funny because of all that.

When you are lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator, do you feel an internal pressure or a sense of dread that forces you to do it, or do you feel like these actions are being controlled by some outside force?

I wouldn't say it's like a dread, or like someone is physically moving my hands for me... it's more about what the numbers actually mean. I know it sounds strange, but I get convinced that certain invoice totals, account numbers, and due dates are actually hidden messages about me. I have to line up the receipts to see them clearly. 

My supervisor, Mr. Davis—he's been at the company forever and he always wears these really loud patterned ties. Like yesterday, he had one with tiny golf clubs all over it, and he doesn't even play golf. He told me he prefers fishing out by the lake on the weekends, usually for bass, though he says the lake has been getting too crowded lately with all those jet skis... anyway, he sits down with me and tries to show me that they are just normal accounting entries. He pulls up the master spreadsheet and points at the columns to prove it. But even when he shows me they are normal, I still feel like they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. 

Which makes me think about tracking numbers, you know? Like when you order a package. I bought this vintage desk lamp on eBay a couple weeks ago, the kind with the green glass shade, like they use in old libraries or banks. The tracking said it was delivered but it took me three days to find it because the mailman put it behind the bushes near the side gate, and it rained, so the cardboard got all mushy. But yeah, I just tap the calculator because I need to figure out the pattern they're sending me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

Yeah, I... I do hear things sometimes. Like when I'm just sitting alone at my desk, or when I'm walking home from my night classes. It's usually a man's voice, and it sounds so real. He'll say things like, "check line seven," or "you missed the sign." It's so clear that I actually stop and look around, but the street is always empty. 

Walking home at night is actually pretty nice, usually. The air gets cooler, and you can smell the jasmine from Mrs. Gable's yard at the corner. She has this huge bush that just takes over the whole fence. She used to give out full-sized candy bars on Halloween, which made her house the best one on the block. But last year she switched to those little boxes of raisins, which, honestly, nobody wants. I mean, they just get stuck in your teeth, and the boxes always get squished at the bottom of the bag. But her garden is still really nice. 

Anyway, yeah, I look around and there's nobody there, just the voice telling me I missed a sign.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about patterns and hearing this voice?

I guess... well, the voices and that feeling that the numbers are actually messages, that's been happening for about eight months now. It started right around the time the weather started getting cold. Which reminds me, I really need to buy a new winter coat. My old one, this heavy wool peacoat I got at a thrift store, it has a hole in the left pocket. I kept losing my keys in the lining, and one time they slid all the way down to the hem, and I had to cut a slit in the bottom just to get them out. The thrift store where I bought it is actually closing down next month, which is a real shame because they always had the best selection of vintage vinyl records. I found an original pressing of a Fleetwood Mac album there once for like two dollars... but yeah, about eight months.
